title: Security Testing

header.html: 5.5 Understand security testing: Security readiness testing (for example blue teaming, purple teaming, red teaming); Application testing (for example vulnerability scanning, static analysis, dynamic analysis, threat modeling); Physical penetration testing (for example phishing, tailgating, impersonation)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

toc.title: Security readiness testing: red, blue and purple teams

html:
1Why test security

Security testing finds weaknesses before attackers do and proves that controls work. Every test needs written authorization and clear rules of engagement: scope, timing, methods allowed and contacts. Testing without permission is a crime.

Exam tip

. Get written permission first. Scope and rules of engagement protect both the tester and the organization.

2Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing

Test Aim How
Vulnerability scan Find and list known weaknesses Automated tool; broad, fast, low risk
Penetration test Prove what an attacker could actually do Skilled people exploit weaknesses; deeper and riskier
Scan type Meaning
Authenticated (credentialed) Scanner logs in; more accurate
Unauthenticated Sees the system like an outsider

Vulnerabilities are scored by severity (for example with CVSS) and handled by risk: fix, mitigate, accept. Scan regularly and after changes.

Penetration test knowledge Meaning
Black box Tester has no inside information
Gray box Partial information
White box Full information (diagrams, code)
Exam tip

. A scan finds weaknesses; a penetration test exploits them. A scan does not prove an attack would work.

3Security readiness testing: red, blue and purple teams

Team Role
Red team Plays the attacker to test detection and response
Blue team Defends: monitors, detects, responds
Purple team Red and blue work together, sharing findings at once to improve defenses

Red team exercises test people, process and technology together, often without warning the defenders (with senior approval). Purple teaming is collaborative and fast learning.

4Application testing

Method What it does When
Static analysis (SAST) Reads the source code without running it Early, during coding
Dynamic analysis (DAST) Tests the running application from outside Test or staging
Vulnerability scanning of dependencies Checks libraries for known flaws Continuous
Threat modeling Thinks like an attacker at design time: what can go wrong? Design phase

Threat modeling often uses STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege). Fixing a flaw is cheapest at design time.

Exam tip

. Static = code at rest. Dynamic = program running. Threat modeling happens before the code is written.

5Physical penetration testing

Physical penetration testing checks building and people controls with authorized attempts to get in or get information.

Tactic Example
Tailgating Following an employee through a secured door
Impersonation Posing as a delivery person, repair technician or manager
Phishing Fake emails (and calls) to trick staff
Lock picking, badge cloning Defeating door controls
Dumpster diving Searching trash for secrets

The tester carries a signed authorization letter (the "get out of jail free" letter) in case of being stopped. Results lead to better locks, badge rules, guard training and awareness.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team runs an automated tool that lists known weaknesses on all servers. What is this?

  • AA penetration test by experts
  • BA vulnerability scan
  • CA red team exercise
  • DA tabletop exercise
Show the answer

Answer: B. An automated search for known weaknesses is a vulnerability scan.

S2Which test tries to exploit weaknesses to show what an attacker could really do?

  • AA configuration baseline review
  • BA policy review by the auditor
  • CA penetration test by skilled testers
  • DAn asset inventory update
Show the answer

Answer: C. A penetration test exploits weaknesses to prove real impact.

S3In a security exercise the attackers and the defenders share what they learn immediately so that defenses improve quickly. Which team approach is this?

  • ARed team, which only attacks
  • BPurple team, which combines both teams
  • CBlue team, which only defends
  • DGray box, which has partial information
Show the answer

Answer: B. A purple team combines red and blue teams to share findings at once.

S4Developers want to find flaws by analyzing the source code before the program is run. Which method is this?

  • ADynamic analysis of the running program
  • BA physical penetration test of the office
  • CStatic analysis of the source code
  • DA tabletop incident response exercise
Show the answer

Answer: C. Static analysis examines the code without running it.

S5The team asks what could go wrong with a new system while it is still being designed. Which activity is this?

  • AVulnerability scanning of the live servers
  • BThreat modeling at design time
  • CPenetration testing of the finished product
  • DChange management after the release
Show the answer

Answer: B. Thinking like an attacker at design time is threat modeling.

S6A tester wearing a delivery uniform follows an employee through a secured door. Which two tactics are used?

  • AImpersonation and tailgating
  • BPhishing and smishing
  • CDumpster diving and shoulder surfing
  • DBaiting and whaling
Show the answer

Answer: A. Posing as a delivery person is impersonation and following through the door is tailgating.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What must be obtained before any security test?

Show the answer

Written authorization with rules of engagement.

R2What is the difference between a scan and a penetration test?

Show the answer

A scan lists weaknesses; a penetration test exploits them.

R3What does the red team do?

Show the answer

Plays the attacker.

R4What is SAST?

Show the answer

Static analysis of source code.

R5What does STRIDE support?

Show the answer

Threat modeling.

R6What is a gray box test?

Show the answer

A test with partial information.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Rules written authorization, scope, rules of engagement
Scan vs pen test scan finds known weaknesses; pen test exploits them
Teams red attacks, blue defends, purple works together
Application static (code), dynamic (running), dependencies, threat modeling (design, STRIDE)
Physical tailgating, impersonation, phishing, badge cloning; signed letter
